evaluated.name: Goodwill Accrual Collision

evaluated.name: Persistent Innovation Low-Noise

evaluated.name: R&D Dominance over Accounting Wedge
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3)), RATIO(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3), ADD(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), at), 3), ABS(MA(RATIO(SUB(ib, oancf), at), 3)))))

evaluated.name: Intangible-Scaled Working-Capital Mismatch
evaluated.expression: MUL(SUMRANK(MA(RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale), 3), RATIO(intan, at)), ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), LAG(at, 1)), 1)))

evaluated.reasoning: Intangible-based business models should generally require less incremental working capital, so a large buildup is more anomalous when the intangible footprint is high. evaluated.name: Intangible Sales Realization
evaluated.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(intan, at)), RANK(WINSOR(ADD(GROWTH(sale, 1), RATIO(recch, LAG(sale, 1))), 1)))
evaluated.hypothesis: Intangible-intensive firms with sales growth supported by receivables collection rather than receivables accumulation subsequently earn higher returns.
evaluated.reasoning: Because recch is negative when receivables increase, adding it to sales growth correctly penalizes revenue accompanied by a receivables buildup and rewards improved collection. evaluated.author: proposer

evaluated.name: Booked-Intangible Cash-Earnings Validation

evaluated.name: Industry-Relative Intangible Cash Validation
evaluated.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(intan, at)), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(oancf, ib), at), 1)))

evaluated.name: Lagged Intangible Cash Payoff

evaluated.name: Innovation Accrual-Dependence Floor

evaluated.name: Intangible Signed Non-Amortization Accrual

evaluated.name: Intangible Revenue Accrual Burden

evaluated.name: R&D-Accrual Offset Smoothing

evaluated.hypothesis: A completed period of persistent R&D investment followed by consistently cash-supported earnings predicts higher returns.

evaluated.name: Dual Earnings Support

critic_notes.rationale: This is essentially a rank-product double-sort of two well-documented anomalies — R&D-increase abnormal returns (Eberhart-Maxwell-Siddique) and the accrual/change-in-accruals anomaly — with no mechanism that isn't delivered by the two legs separately, so it is more a rediscovery-combination than a new cross-theme insight.

It is Sloan's working-capital accrual anomaly with a coarse high-R&D gate, and the INDICATOR construction hard-zeros ~70% of the cross-section, so quantile portfolios and the FM slope will be dominated by a mass of exact ties rather than by the claimed conditional effect.

The goodwill-addition × accrual interaction is a coherent and reasonably distinct earnings-quality mechanism with sign-consistent construction, though it inherits overlap with the acquisition/asset-growth anomaly and will suffer thin, lumpy coverage because DELTA(gdwl) is zero or missing for most firm-years.

Internally inconsistent sign convention — Compustat recch is the cash-flow item that is negative when receivables build, so SUB(GROWTH(sale), recch/lag(sale)) rewards rather than penalizes receivables accumulation, inverting the stated "receivables-adjusted" hypothesis.

Multiplying raw levels makes the signal essentially cash-flow-to-assets (a known cash-based profitability anomaly largely spanned by FF5's RMW) shrunk by a bounded intangible-share multiplier, so it is both a near-rediscovery and poorly scaled relative to a rank-interaction version.

Conditioning long-horizon R&D intensity on the stability of the earnings-to-cash reconciliation is an economically sensible and reasonably novel "quality of the innovation program" interaction, though both legs echo known R&D-intensity and earnings-volatility effects and the 5-year VOL window will materially reduce coverage.

This is a pure window tweak (5→3 periods) on the archive's "Persistent Innovation Low-Noise" signal with an identical mechanism and no new economic content, and the stated motivation (coverage) is dubious since the archived version already had comparable coverage at 0.081.

Industry-neutralizing both legs is a defensible, diagnosis-driven change to the archived cash-earnings validation signal because it converts a partly sectoral intangible-intensity tilt into a within-peer comparison, though it remains a close derivative whose incremental information is likely modest.

Adding back dp mechanically reduces ib−oancf to roughly working-capital accruals, so the absolute-value transform discards precisely the accrual sign that produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional evidence (fmb −3.11 on the signed intangible×working-capital interaction) and collapses the signal into a generic Dechow–Dichev-style accrual-magnitude/earnings-quality proxy.

The lead-lag construction (prior intangible investment, subsequent cash-flow improvement) is a genuinely different test from the archive's contemporaneous intangible-level interactions, though multiplying two ascending ranks loads the long leg with high asset-growth firms whose known negative asset-growth effect works against the expected positive sign.

This is a recombination of the already-rejected "Goodwill Accrual Collision" (fmb −1.48, alpha ≈ 0) that swaps levels for changes on each leg without diagnosing why the original failed, and the goodwill/at leg is largely a known acquisition-intensity/asset-growth proxy.

Because xrd appears in both legs, the product is dominated by squared R&D intensity plus depreciation scaling (ib−oancf ≈ ΔWC − dp), so the signal does not cleanly test the stated "cash before R&D versus earnings" mechanism and largely rediscovers the known R&D-intensity effect; the mismatched scalers (xrd/sale vs xrd/at) compound this.

The expression matches the hypothesis (a non-negative R&D rank scaling a signed 5-year accrual trend, so a rising accrual-dependence trend maps to the predicted negative direction) and the trend framing is a genuine directional variation on the archive's level/volatility/minimum treatments of the same R&D×accrual pair, though it remains a close member of that family and the second leg is close to the known change-in-accruals effect.

The claimed investment-to-realization timing test is not actually implemented, since LAG of a 3-year moving average of R&D/sales overlaps two-thirds with the contemporaneous window and is nearly indistinguishable from plain R&D intensity, leaving the signal an incremental rewrite of the archive's lagged-intangible and cash-validation composites.

The recch sign convention is handled correctly and the bounded scaling by |recch|+|Δsale| is a substantively different construction from the failed sales-growth composite, though the underlying receivables-accrual effect is well documented and the ratio can be noisy when both sales and receivables changes are near zero.

Since Compustat intan includes goodwill, Δintan−xrd interacted with signed accruals is largely a re-parameterization of the archive's already-tested and failed Goodwill Accrual Collision, with the added R&D subtraction unlikely to change the acquisition/asset-growth channel that drives it.

Swapping the conditioning variable from booked intangibles (which conflate acquisitions and amortization) to persistent R&D intensity is a defensible diagnosis-driven change rather than a cosmetic tweak, and the depreciation add-back correctly isolates working-capital accruals in line with the stated hypothesis, though it is still a modest edit of an already weak archive signal.

This is a single-theme rescaling of the long-known R&D-intensity anomaly rather than a cross-theme interaction, and COALESCE(xrd,0) creates a large point mass at exactly zero so the industry rank mostly just separates R&D reporters from non-reporters.

A defensible diagnostic edit on the archive's strongest signal — swapping the cash-minus-earnings trend for a pure operating-cash-profitability trend genuinely tests whether the payoff comes from cash realization rather than accrual reversal — but it sits close to the known R&D-intensity × profitability-improvement combination and risks being an incremental variant rather than a new mechanism.

The sign logic is internally consistent (both offsetting quadrants yield a positive product, predicting low returns), and it is not a level-based rediscovery, but it is a noisy double-difference that lumps "R&D up + accruals up" (which may simply be growth-driven) with "R&D cut + accruals down," so the economic interpretation of the long-short spread will be hard to attribute.

Sign conventions on the cash-flow-statement items are handled correctly (recch/invch negative on asset build-ups, apalch positive on payable increases) and the absolute-flow denominator is a sensible scale control, but this is the third attempt in the archive at R&D/intangible-intensity × working-capital accruals, the prior two of which failed on either slope or alpha, so the decomposition needs to carry a lot of weight to be more than a re-slicing of the accruals anomaly.

Reframing the strongest archived negative signal as an episodic within-firm accounting transition is a genuine and well-motivated diagnosis of its weak linear slope versus strong alpha, but TS_RANK over a 3-observation window is extremely coarse (effectively three levels) and discards cross-sectional information, so the refinement may amount mostly to re-scaling one leg.

This is the minimal edit to the archived "Booked-Intangible Cash-Earnings Validation" (intan/at → (intan-gdwl)/at) with an identical second leg, and the goodwill-versus-organic distinction has already been probed by the archived "Organic-over-Acquired Cash Validation," so it is a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively different mechanism.

The signal is a SUMRANK blend of the left legs of two already-evaluated signals multiplied by their shared cash-minus-earnings leg, so its performance is mechanically bounded between the two archived results; worse, it averages a high-expensing indicator with a high-capitalized-intangible indicator, which are conceptually opposed accounting regimes, muddying rather than sharpening the mechanism.

Economically motivated purification of the archive's strongest signal (subtracting payable and tax-accrual financing from operating cash is directionally consistent with the hypothesis), but it is an incremental variant whose main risk is a sharp coverage drop from apalch/txach availability (prior apalch-based signals ran ~0.057 versus 0.090 here), so the true test is whether the slope survives on the narrower sample.

This is close to a mechanical recombination of two archive signals (lagged R&D leg from "Nonoverlapping R&D Cash Realization" plus the TS_MIN cash-reconciliation leg from "Innovation Accrual-Dependence Floor"), but substituting a durability floor for a trend is a genuinely different economic claim (persistent level versus improvement) and the construction is internally consistent with the positive expected sign.

The quadrant restriction is a coherent and internally consistent earnings-management mechanism (both RANK legs increase with R&D cuts and rising accruals, so high values map to the predicted underperformance), though it inherits substantial overlap with the accrual anomaly and with the earlier offset-smoothing signal, and the RANK×RANK product leaves the low end economically ambiguous.

This stacks the legs of two already-tested archive signals whose Fama-MacBeth slopes were both insignificant, double-counts dp (once inside the non-amortization accrual and again in the DELTA(dp/at) term), and is explicitly motivated by hoping the union will "align" prior mismatched evidence — i.e., specification search rather than a new mechanism.

Rescaling cash to gross profit is a legitimately different economic question from the asset-scaled cash floor and the 3-year aggregation is sensible, but the denominator (sale−cogs) can be small or negative, so low/negative-gross-profit firms will produce sign-flipped extreme ratios that winsorization only partly tames and that muddy the ranking's interpretation.

A coherent single-scale composite that extends the archive's pre-R&D cash surplus by netting identifiable-intangible capitalization, and the sign logic is consistent, but the equal, unmotivated weighting of the capitalization term against the cash-earnings wedge and the unexplained drop from IND_ZSCORE to plain ZSCORE make it hard to attribute any result to the new ingredient.

This is a mechanical recombination of two archived signals — the identical R&D/(R&D+DP) expensing leg from "Cash-Validated Expense Mix" paired with the TS_MIN floor construction from "Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor" — so its likely outcome (a modest ~2–3 t-stat alpha) is largely already known and it adds little beyond a diagnostic swap of level profitability for the accrual wedge.

This is a cosmetic re-normalization of the already-tested "Innovation Gross-Profit Cash Conversion" (which already delivered ls_talpha 3.08), and the |gross profit| in the denominator actually distorts the economics by assigning high conversion scores to negative-gross-profit firms with positive cash flow.

The ABS on the three-year change in non-goodwill intangibles contradicts the stated hypothesis, since large amortization-driven *declines* in booked intangibles are penalized identically to capitalization, and the signal otherwise closely overlaps the archived "Organic-over-Acquired Cash Validation" with the same cash-validation leg.

Swapping RANK for ZSCORE on the cash-deterioration leg is a thin change, but it is a legitimately motivated response to the archived signal's strong-alpha/weak-slope divergence, since it makes the interaction signed rather than uniformly positive and shrinks capitalization-neutral firms toward zero.

The sign convention on invch is handled correctly and the conjunction is internally consistent and distinct from the archive, though both legs are individually known anomalies (R&D declines, inventory growth) so the composite risks simply loading on inventory growth rather than the claimed dual expense-deferral channel.

The bounded cash-coverage leg is well-constructed and the deliberate mechanical tension between the two legs is a sensible way to isolate sustainably funded innovation, but the R&D-intensity × cash-strength family has already been mined heavily in this archive so incremental information is likely limited.

This is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested archive signals ("R&D Cash-Absorption Capacity" for the bounded cash/R&D coverage leg and "Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor" for the TS_MIN floor operator), so it adds a cosmetic operator swap rather than a new mechanism, and the TS_MIN of a bounded ratio will be dominated by a single loss-year outlier.

Identical to the archived "Accrual-Adjusted Innovation Margin" with MA(...,3) replaced by TS_MIN(...,3) — a one-operator variant of a signal that already worked, offering little incremental economic information and likely high correlation with the original.

critic_notes.target_name: Organic Cash Surplus with Low Capitalization
critic_notes.rationale: Decomposing the archived net-support composite into separately ranked legs with a MAX(·,0) capitalization floor is a defensible, economically motivated re-specification rather than a cosmetic tweak, though the zero-capitalization mass will produce heavy rank ties in the second leg and the surviving predictive content may still come almost entirely from the already-tested pre-R&D cash surplus.

The expression's direction is internally consistent with the stated hypothesis and the netted earnings-versus-cash disconnect is a genuinely single-construct signal, but it imposes an arbitrary one-for-one weight and is at risk of being largely a repackaging of the well-known change-in-cash-flow/profitability and investment-decline effects.

The nonoverlapping lagged-R&D template has already been tested three times in the archive (cash-reconciliation trend, operating-cash trend, organic-formation), and swapping in the accrual-adjusted margin trend — itself already used in another archive signal — is a leg substitution within a saturated family rather than a substantively new mechanism.

Pure DELTA→TREND operator swap on the archived "Dual Expense Compression" with an already-weak economic story, since declining dp/at is largely mechanical asset-mix and the R&D leg is close to the known investment/R&D-decline anomaly.

This is essentially the archived "R&D Pre-Working-Capital Cash Generation" leg with `ib` subtracted and RANK swapped for ZSCORE, which merely re-splices it onto the already-archived (oancf − ib) accrual leg rather than testing a genuinely new mechanism.

Internally consistent (recch/invch signs correctly penalize working-capital absorption), but it overlaps two archived signals — "Accrual-Adjusted Innovation Margin" and "Incremental R&D Commercialization Payback" — with the only real change being the scaling denominator, so it reads as a cosmetic rescaling rather than a new economic idea.

The two legs are near-mechanically linked (xrd and dp are deductions in ib, so falling expense intensity arithmetically lifts ROA), and the negative expected sign fights the well-documented positive predictive direction of Δ profitability, making the construct partly tautological and directionally ambiguous.

A coherent recombination that gates the archived "R&D Cut with Slower Intangible Amortization" leg on actual identifiable-intangible growth — a defensible sharpening of the delayed-recognition mechanism — though it is incremental and the triple-rank product plus MIN gate risks correlated, thinner-coverage results very close to the two archived parents.

The signed gross-margin-minus-cash-margin divergence is a substantively different second leg from the archived expense-versus-cash disconnect and the sign logic matches the hypothesis, though the underlying accounting-versus-cash wedge is close to the classic Sloan channel and only the R&D-cut conditioning supplies the novelty.

The materiality concern about low-depreciation firms is legitimate, but adding a MIN gate to the archived "Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor" (already fmb 4.54, alpha 5.2%, talpha 3.85) is a gating tweak whose output will be highly correlated with the parent, so it is more a robustness check than a new signal.

The weakest-link MIN is internally coherent and the invariance argument is correct (a receivables build raises the pre-working-capital cash term while lowering the adjusted-margin term, so the composite cannot be gamed by one working-capital swing), but it is still largely a blend of two already-strong archived signals and should be judged on whether it beats both, not merely on being positive.

This is structurally the archived "Persistent Innovation Low-Noise" signal (R&D intensity × NEG volatility of a fundamental ratio) with the volatility target swapped, and it also overlaps the well-documented earnings/fundamental-volatility anomaly, while a three-observation VOL is too short to measure stability reliably.

Beyond being the bounded-ratio restatement of the archived "Organic Investment Net Accounting Support" contrast, the construction is degenerate — whenever the pre-R&D cash surplus is negative the numerator equals the denominator, pinning a large mass of firms at exactly 1 and destroying cross-sectional discrimination in precisely the distressed region the hypothesis cares about.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it recombines the same three archived ingredients (R&D cut, positive identifiable-intangible additions, weak amortization recognition) already tested twice with similar results, making it a cosmetic reparameterization rather than a new mechanism.

This is the archived best signal ("Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor") with the cash measure adjusted again, and the directly analogous prior attempt ("Liability-Adjusted Expensing Cash Floor") already showed this class of adjustment degrades the alpha and coverage without a diagnosed economic reason for a different outcome here.

Signing the previously absolute-valued reconciliation gap is a legitimate, diagnosis-motivated refinement with a coherent quality-of-cash-flow story and a consistent expected sign, though dpc−dp differences are substantially definitional/data artifacts, so the economic interpretation is weak and the result should be scrutinized for mechanical drivers.

This is a mechanical splice of two already-archived legs — the expense-mix ratio from "Expensing-Regime Cash Funding Floor" and the (oancf−dpc)/at leg from "Depreciation-Addback-Free Innovation Cash" — and since both conditioning legs proxy the same R&D-heaviness construct, it is a cosmetic variant rather than a new mechanism.

Identical in structure to the archived "Working-Capital-Invariant Innovation Realization" with only "−dpc" appended to the cash leg, which is a one-term tweak of an existing strong signal rather than a substantively different hypothesis, and stacking dpc, recch and invch subtractions on top of a margin leg that already re-adds recch/invch double-counts the same adjustments.

This is the archived "Accrual-Adjusted Innovation Margin" with xrd/sale subtracted from the second leg, and because that subtraction is mechanically the negative of the first leg the product partly cancels itself, making the economic interpretation (R&D productivity vs. R&D intensity) ambiguous rather than sharper.

The pairing of intangible-to-equity fragility with a declining amortization-recognition rate is an untested combination whose sign and expression are internally consistent, though both legs are recycled from archived signals and share intan−gdwl in numerator and denominator, so the mechanical overlap should be diagnosed if results look strong.

This is the archived "Intangible Equity Fragility with Accrual Support" with the accrual leg swapped for a negated cash-profitability leg, and since oancf−dpc scaled by assets is essentially a cash-profitability sort, the signal risks rediscovering the well-known profitability/distress effect conditioned on intangible intensity.

The archive already contains two versions of "capitalization migration plus weak cash" ("Nonoverlapping Capitalization Cash Failure", "R&D-to-Capitalized Migration Support"), and replacing the cash-trend leg with an addback-free cash level is an incremental leg swap rather than a diagnosis-driven redirection.
